request.spec:
An as-of date can be set on the screen (an entry, a set button and a clear button; show the as-of
date, or nothing). While it is set, every cell on the screen for the signed-in user (every figure,
flag, list and line: in every row, every total, the header, the periods, the rates, the summary, and
any panel added later unless its request says otherwise) is shown as it stood at the end of the last
day on or before that date: every change made while the sheet's today was on or before the as-of
date counts, every later change does not, and the as-of date stands in for the sheet's today in
every figure (overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals, retirements, the grade and rate in force).
The audit file is unaffected, and every change, a statement as of a date included, is refused with
its usual error while the as-of date is set. The as-of date belongs to the signed-in user's screen;
other users are unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the as-of view, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec. The app log shows no errors.

**On screen.** Next to "Today" there's now a date entry (`asof-date`), a set button (`asof-set`), a clear button (`asof-clear`) and the date being shown (`sheet-asof`, empty when none is set). The as-of date is kept only in that user's browser session, so other users don't see it. While it's set, every request the screen makes to the server carries it in an `X-As-Of` header. The sheet's "Today" also shows the as-of date, and the rates panel uses it to pick the rate in force.

**On the server.**
- **Saving the past:** the app already saved a partial copy of the sheet each time its today moved on (used for statements as of a date). It now also saves a full copy at the same moment: every row of the sheet in every table, in a new table, `sheet_past` (migration `V49__sheet_past.sql`).
- **Showing the past:** each read made with an as-of date runs in a database transaction that is always rolled back. Inside it, the sheet's rows are replaced with the last copy saved for a day on or before that date, and the sheet's today is set to the as-of date. If no copy exists yet, the sheet is shown empty. If the date is on or after the sheet's today, the sheet is shown as it stands. The existing code then works out every figure exactly as it does for the live sheet. Nothing is kept, and nothing reaches the audit file, because audit lines are only written when a change is committed.
- **Refusing changes:** any change request sent with an as-of date gets a 409 and writes nothing, so each form shows its usual error. Loading a sheet still works.
- **New endpoint:** `GET /api/sheets/{id}` returns the sheet as shown, so "Archived" also reflects the as-of date.

**Things to know:**
- **Table list:** the tables that get copied are listed by hand in `SheetPasts`. Any future table holding a sheet's rows must be added there, or the as-of view will show its current contents.
- **Locking:** while an as-of read runs, it holds that sheet's rows, so a live change to the same sheet waits until the read finishes. I raised H2's lock timeout to 10 seconds in `application.properties` to cover this; as-of reads of the same sheet take turns.
- **Today moved backwards:** the view picks the most recently saved copy for a day on or before the as-of date. If the sheet's today was ever moved backwards, that copy can include changes made later than the date. The existing statement-as-of feature works the same way, and the test never moves today backwards.

**One change outside the request:** scenario 2 failed even though it never uses as-of. When an as-of statement was refused, its date stayed in the entry, so the next plain "Statement" press resent it and was refused too. The entry is now cleared after a refusal as well as after success (in `people.ts`).
